chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim, from 'Ali, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, that he said:
Regarding the Muslim shaking hands with the Jew and the Christian, he said: "From behind the clothes; and if he shakes your hand with his hand, then wash your hand."

key_terms.الثِّيَابِ: garments or clothing serving as a barrier
key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيِّ: the Christian person with whom the interaction occurs
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِ: the Muslim person addressed in the ruling
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْ: then wash; an instruction to cleanse
key_terms.لِلْيَهُودِيِّ: the Jewish person with whom the interaction occurs
key_terms.يَدَكَ: your hand, the limb affected by direct contact

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith in Tahdhib al-Ahkam say about shaking hands with a Jew or a Christian?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning physical contact with a Jew or a Christian in the context discussed in the chapter on purification from najasah. It instructs that such handshaking should be done from behind a garment, and if direct hand contact occurs, the hand should be washed.
